why: The canonical 'take the best two, push the result back' heap loop: always join the two shortest ropes, because every rope's length is paid again in every later join it takes part in (Huffman's argument).
hints: Every join's cost is paid again by each later join that includes the result. Which ropes should be joined early, then?
Always join the two shortest ropes currently available, then treat the result as a new rope.
heapify the lengths; while more than one: pop a, pop b, cost += a + b, push a + b. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Sorting once is not enough: the joined rope must re-enter the order, which is what the heap is for.
